answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond that is slashed if it double-votes or breaks a task’s rules. Honest agents recover the bond after a dispute window, but an attacker must lock real capital in every fake account and risks losing it when evidence links coordinated behavior. Making identities costly limits how many votes a sybil can buy; saffron, nectar, and ripple can label sample tasks, but the bond—not the labels—provides the economic deterrent.
